'''Suresh Rattan''' (full name: '''''Suresh Inder Singh Rattan'''''; born in 1955 in [[Amritsar]], India) is a [[Biogerontologist#Biogerontology|biogerontologist]] – a researcher in the field of biology of ageing, [[biogerontology]].

In addition to his professional research work on the biology of [[ageing]], he is also very much interested and involved in the public communication of science<ref name="auto">{{cite web | title = Dr. Suresh Rattan  | work = Books by Dr. Suresh I.S. Rattan | url = http://www.sureshrattan.com/books.html | access-date = 27 April 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080308142708/http://www.sureshrattan.com/books.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 8 March 2008}}</ref> and he likes to undertake explorations in the [[Indian classical music]] and semi-classical music by playing [[Tabla]] – the North Indian drums, as evident from music CDs "State of the Art: Small Town People" by Harry Jokumsen and other artists (2008), and "The Fall and the Rise of a Woman" by Pearl (2014) in which he plays Tabla under his artistic name Shashi Maharaj.<ref>{{cite web|title=Edgehogmusic|url=http://www.harryjokumsen.dk/english/edgehogmusicuk.html}}</ref>

==Academic background==
Suresh Rattan has been heading, since its inception in 1984, the Laboratory of Cellular Ageing at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics<ref>{{cite web | title = Molekylærbiologisk Institut  | work = ( Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics) | url = http://www.mbg.au.dk  | access-date = 27 April 2008 }}</ref> at the [[Aarhus University]] in Denmark, where he has become Emeritus since 2020. He was introduced to the field of ageing by Professor Suraj P. Sharma at the [[Guru Nanak Dev University]] (GNDU), [[Amritsar]], [[India]], during his BSc and MSc studies (1973–1977), followed by MPhil studies on the regenerative capacity of Hydra, under the guidance of Professor Sivatosh Mookerjee, at the School of Life Sciences, [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] (JNU), New Delhi, India (1977–1979). Suresh Rattan earned his PhD in 1982 from the [[National Institute for Medical Research]], Mill Hill, London, UK, based on his research project testing the error theory of cellular ageing, under the supervision of Dr. [[Robin Holliday]] FRS, and Dr. Ian Buchanan. He also earned the degree of Doctor of Science (DSc) in 1995, from the Faculty of Natural Sciences, University of Aarhus, Denmark, based on his post-PhD research work on the molecular biology of human cellular ageing. He is also the recipient of an [https://web.archive.org/web/20101128205922/http://mb.au.dk/en/single-news/article/suresh-rattan-nominated-honorary-doctor-at-the-russian-academy-of-medical-sciences/ Honorary Doctorate] from the Russian Academy of Medical Sciences for his "...fruitful research and training in the field of biology of ageing, as well as his outstanding contribution to dissemination of scientific knowledge in basic gerontology...". He has been awarded a Visiting Professorship at the Faculty of Science, [http://www.upol.cz/en/ Palacky University in Olomouc, Czech Republic] (2012–2016). The [[British Society for Research on Ageing]] (BSRA) has awarded their prestigious [[Lord Cohen Medal]] to Suresh Rattan for his continuing contributions to gerontology.<ref>[[British Society for Research on Ageing (BSRA)]]</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=21 March 2011|url=http://mb.au.dk/en/single-news/article/suresh-rattan-awarded-the-lord-cohen-medal-in-gerontology/|title=Suresh Rattan awarded the Lord Cohen Medal in gerontology|date=9 March 2011|publisher=Department of Molecular Biology, [[Aarhus Faculty of Science and Technology (Aarhus University)|Faculty of Science, Aarhus University]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110312002024/http://mb.au.dk/en/single-news/article/suresh-rattan-awarded-the-lord-cohen-medal-in-gerontology/|archive-date=12 March 2011|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He was unanimously elected as the President/Chair of the Biological Section of the European Region of the [[International Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics]] ([[IAGG-ER]]) for the periods 2011–2015, 2015 to 2019, and again for the period 2019–2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.iagg-er.net/ |access-date=15 December 2012 |publisher=Aarhus Universitet |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120321060755/http://mb.au.dk/en/single-news/artikel/international-recognition-for-suresh-rattan/ |archive-date=21 March 2012 |df=dmy-all |title=International recognition for Suresh Rattan }}</ref> He was given the Outstanding Career Achievement Award - 2017, by the International Dose Response Society, USA <ref>http://dose-response.org/2017-awards/></ref> and the Lifetime Acheivement Award by the NUS Healthy Longevity Academy, Singapore, 2026<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy for Healthy Longevity |url=https://longevityacademy.sg/ |access-date=2026-11-10 |website=longevityacademy.sg |language=en}}</ref>

Suresh Rattan has published over 300 research and review articles<ref>{{cite web | title = Dr. Suresh Rattan  | work = List of publications by Dr. Suresh I.S. Rattan | url = http://www.sureshrattan.com/publications.html | access-date = 27 April 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080308135221/http://www.sureshrattan.com/publications.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 8 March 2008}}</ref> 
and about 20 books<ref name="auto"/> on the biology of ageing, including those for school children and general public. He is the founding Editor-in-Chief of ''[[Biogerontology (journal)|Biogerontology]]'',<ref>{{cite web | title = BIOGERONTOLOGY  | work = [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer Publishing]] | url = https://www.springer.com/journal/10522/editors | access-date = 23 March 2023 }}</ref> a leading peer reviewed journal in the field of ageing. His name has been included in [[Marquis Who's Who|Marquis Who's Who in the World ]](from 1993);<ref>{{cite web | title = Marquis Who's Who in the World | url = http://www.marquiswhoswho.com/products/WOprodinfo.asp | access-date = 27 April 2008 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080514205745/http://www.marquiswhoswho.com/products/WOprodinfo.asp | archive-date = 14 May 2008 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> Marquis Who's Who in Medicine and Healthcare (from 1998); and International Directory of Distinguished Leadership (from 1998). He was a member of the [[World Economic Forum]]'s Global Agenda Council on Gerontology (2008–2009).

==Important contributions==
Suresh Rattan's major intellectual contribution in [[gerontology]] is the formulation of the concepts of essential lifespan and virtual gerontogenes<ref>{{cite journal |journal = FASEB J. | title = Gerontogenes: real or virtual?|date=1995| doi=10.1096/fasebj.9.2.7781932|last = Rattan | first = S I| volume = 9| issue = 2| pages = 284–286| doi-access = free| pmid = 7781932| s2cid = 22407928}}</ref> 
regarding the nature of genes involved in ageing that real gerontogenes do not exist. Additionally, in the area of ageing modulation, Suresh Rattan is credited with the sole inventorship for discovering the anti-ageing effects of 
[[kinetin]]<ref>{{US patent reference  | number = 5602139  | y = 1997  | m = 02  | d = 11  | inventor = Suresh Rattan  | title =  Method for ameliorating the adverse effects of aging }}</ref> and [[zeatin]] in human skin cells; and these compounds are being used in several skin-care cosmetics throughout the world, for example [[Valeant]] product [[Kinerase]].
His areas of expertise include ageing, anti-ageing and healthy ageing of human cells, specially [[fibroblasts]], [[keratinocytes]], [[osteoblasts]], and bone marrow [[stem cells]]. His current research focuses on the beneficial effects of mild stress, [[Hormesis]], and discovering hormetins (a new category of natural and synthetic compounds which bring about their beneficial effects through hormesis) for slowing down ageing and improving the quality of life in old age. The first skincare product to come out of the theory of hormesis is the [http://www.stylelist.com/2010/08/30/givenchy-vaxin-for-youth/ Vaxin for Youth from Givenchy]. He has also put forward the terms for the science and study of hormesis, and "hormetin" for any condition that can bring about hormesis "[http://sureshrattan.com/ hormetics]".

==Books==
Suresh Rattan has written/edited/co-edited the following books on ageing in English, Punjabi and Danish:

=== In English ===
* Supplemets and Drugs for Health and Longevity, Editors: Suresh I.S. Rattan and Ceren Gezer; volume 22 in the book series “Healthy Ageing and Longevity”, Springer Nature, Switzerland, 2026; [[Special:BookSources/9783032116079|ISBN 978-3-032-11607-9]]
* Brain and Mental Health in Ageing, Editors: Gurcharan Kaur and Suresh I.S. Rattan; volume 21 in the book series “Healthy Ageing and Longevity”, Springer Nature, Switzerland, 2024; ISBN 978-3-031-68512-5
* Successful Ageing: Ambition and Ambivalence, Authors: Clemens Tesch-Romer,  Hans-Werner Wahl,  Suresh I.S. Rattan, and Liat Ayalon; Oxford University Press, UK; 2021 {{ISBN|9780192897534}}
* Nutrition, Food and Diet in Ageing and Longevity, Editors: Suresh I.S. Rattan and Gurcharan Kaur; volume 14 in the book series "Healthy Ageing and Longevity", Springer Nature, Switzerland, 2021 {{ISBN|978-3-030-83016-8}}
* Explaining Health Across the Sciences, Editors: Jonathan Sholl and Suresh I.S. Rattan; volume 12 in the book series "Healthy Ageing and Longevity", Springer Nature, Switzerland, 2020 {{ISBN|978-3-030-52663-4}}
* Encyclopedia of Biomedical Gerontology, Editor-in-Chief: Suresh I.S. Rattan; 3 volumes, Elsevier/Academic Press; 2020 {{ISBN|978-0-12-816075-6}}
* The Science of Hormesis in Health and Longevity, Academic Press UK; 2019 {{ISBN|978-3-319-63000-7}}
* AGE, in the series Reflections, by Aarhus University Press, 2018 {{ISBN|978-87-7184-735-2}}
* Hormones in Ageing and Longevity, 2017 {{ISBN|978-3-319-63000-7}} {{doi|10.1007/978-3-319-63001-4}}
* Cellular Ageing and Replicative Senescence, 2016 ({{ISBN|978-3-319-26237-6}} [https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783319262376])
* Hormesis in Health and Disease, 2014 ({{ISBN|978-148-2205459}})
* Brain Aging and Therapeutic Interventions, 2012 ({{ISBN|978-94-007-5236-8}})
* Calorie Restriction, Aging, and Longevity, 2010 ({{ISBN|978-90-481-8555-9}})
* Mild Stress and Healthy Aging: Applying hormesis in ageing research and interventions, 2008 ({{ISBN|978-1-4020-6868-3}})
* Healthy Aging and Longevity, 2007 ({{ISBN|978-1-57331-680-4}})
* Biogerontology: Mechanisms and Interventions, 2007 ({{ISBN|978-1-57331-679-8}})
* Prevention and Treatment of Age-related Diseases ({{ISBN|978-1-4020-4884-5}})
* Understanding and Modulating Aging, 2006 ({{ISBN|978-1-57331-599-9}})
* Aging Interventions and Therapies, 2005 ({{ISBN|981-256-084-X}})
* Biological Aging and Its Modulation, 2003 ({{ISBN|1-4020-1369-8}})
* Molecular Gerontology: Research Status and Strategies, 1996 ({{ISBN|0-306-45491-2}})
* Where's Baba Gone?, 1999, 2001, 2012 ({{ISBN|81-87510-20-X}})-'' a popular science-in-fiction book for children.'', also published in Punjabi 
(Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi scripts), Hindi (Devnagri script), Polish and Romanian languages.
